findings.finding: A synthetic generic quadruped can be authored through the existing single-asset PixelProgram/Canvas path and accepted by the human owner without a creature-specific raster engine.
The retained 32x32 output communicates four supports, right-facing pose, tail, light/shadow separation, and a simple ground shadow sufficiently for the approved generic creature fixture.
The accepted retained output required one real provider call with 18,854 input tokens and 3,762 output tokens; P10 does not erase the previously retained B1 staged-cost warning.
Creature promotion added no hidden scheduler provider call, morphology-research provider call, regeneration call, or second raster authority.
The successful retained attempt needed no human-requested repair, canvas restart, or regeneration provider call after deterministic QA converged.
Human perceptual acceptance remains separate from deterministic QA; recognizability, stylized anatomy, pose readability, and visual coherence are not converted into deterministic truth.
